children: Oil prices are flashing a supply signal after Saudi Arabia reported that its crude production collapsed in August to the lowest level since 1990 as regional conflict disrupted export routes.

The kingdom told OPEC that output fell by 1.9 million barrels per day to 6.23 million, a 23% decline from July. Saudi crude exports also dropped to 3.1 million barrels per day from 5.1 million, reaching their lowest level since at least 2013, according to Kpler.
West Texas Intermediate crude oil futures jumped 3% Thursday as traders reacted to intensifying attacks on Middle Eastern shipping and energy infrastructure.
Why Saudi Arabia's Drop Matters for Oil Prices

The disruption reflects an increasingly dangerous transportation bottleneck. Saudi Arabia relied on Red Sea routes after the conflict with Iran effectively closed the Strait of Hormuz. Houthi rebels then declared a maritime embargo on Saudi ports, deterring ship operators and restricting another major export corridor.

The Houthis have since intensified strikes against Saudi energy facilities and reportedly seized Yemen's port city of Mocha. That development could increase risks surrounding the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a critical passage connecting the Red Sea with global markets.

OPEC's broader numbers provide one important counterpoint. Total production across the cartel rose by 346,000 barrels per day to 24.1 million in August, even as Iranian output declined by 399,000 barrels per day to 2.1 million.

That means the strongest bullish signal comes from export vulnerability rather than a uniform production collapse across OPEC. If Saudi shipments remain constrained, traders may continue adding a geopolitical premium to crude prices.

Investors can monitor the United States Oil Fund, United States Brent Oil Fund and Energy Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLE) for market reactions. The next decisive signals will be Saudi export volumes, shipping activity through Bab el-Mandeb and Hormuz, and whether attacks spread to additional oil infrastructure.

title: Oil Prices Flash Strong Signal as Saudi Output Collapses
